decisions.reason: The fifteen-day program needs little dedicated investment and sits close to the core offer, so management keeps it, though its overlap with express line D leaves some risk that it is folded in.
The seventy-two-hour promise is costly to sustain but supports the publicly stated fast-response positioning, so management keeps it and attributes weak uptake to temporary market conditions.
The firm launched the door publicly at BAU, invested in its European approval and built it into the core Teckentrup 62 system, so it will persist with it.
The multi-model express line has its own page and anchors the firm's visible fast-delivery commitment, so withdrawal is unlikely.
The digital platform carries substantial sunk development costs and is central to the announced service direction, so shortfalls would be treated as start-up difficulties.
The fire and smoke protection door belongs to the certified core safety portfolio, and its approval investment makes dropping it unlikely.
